target_customer: Banks, credit unions, independent mortgage bankers and mortgage servicers with large call centers and manual back office work
problem: Mortgage servicers and lenders run payment collection, servicing calls and loan origination steps manually at high cost, and their legacy core systems are hard to replace.
business_model: B2B AI agents sold as an AI workforce (KastleOS) on top of existing systems, priced per deployment with dedicated engineering support
product_category: AI agents for regulated financial operations

founders.name: Rishi Choudhary
education: BS Systems Engineering, University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign
founders.background_notes: Founding product manager for Redfin's Mortgage Marketplace, grew revenue from $3M to $6M in nine months, led Redfin Search Experience.

founders.name: Nitish Poddar
education: Computer Science, University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign
founders.background_notes: Tech lead at Verkada on a patented motion search system and backend inference infrastructure. Some sources spell the first name Nitesh.

technical_complexity.rationale: Voice and SMS agents with compliance logic (FDCPA, RESPA, TCPA) and integrations into servicing and telephony systems are standard engineering with hard parts around accuracy and escalation in a regulated setting.

defensibility.rationale: Deep integrations with servicing systems, compliance scoring and named mortgage servicer customers create stickiness, while general voice agent platforms can be reconfigured by competitors.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Specialist voice AI vendors for lender collections grew in parallel (for example Salient reportedly reached $25M ARR). No incumbent has acquired or displaced Kastle as of the research date.

market_need_then: The founders found through outreach that about 10 million Americans make mortgage payments by phone each month, and call center costs are a large expense for servicers. Their own claim is a 90 percent reduction in call center cost.

branding.domain_note: Uses kastle.ai, spelled with a K, likely because castle domains were taken. Kastle Systems is an older unrelated company with a similar name.

identity.logo: A refined castle icon with bold clean typography according to a Bluetext agency case study, which may refer to a different Kastle
identity.mascot_or_character: Five named AI agents: Alex, Patricia, Avery, Leslie and Sage
identity.voice_and_tone: Confident, direct and compliance minded, for example correctness first automation at scale

branding.brand_signature: Named AI employees for each role, framed as an AI full time employee
branding.community_and_virality: No merch or community found. Trade press covers the Series A and a YC Root Access interview exists.

brand_strength.rationale: A memorable, trust signalling name and a coherent agent persona system for a regulated buyer, with wide fintech trade coverage of the funding, though no consumer community and a confusable spelling.

outcome_analysis: Kastle started with AI voice agents for mortgage servicing in Summer 2024, expanded to originations and fulfillment, and raised a $24M Series A in September 2026 led by Insight Partners after landing servicers such as Newrez and Carrington. Founders with Redfin mortgage experience, a regulated niche with large call center spend and the LLM voice tailwind explain the traction. It remains Active and no exit has occurred.
notes: Series A is reported by many outlets (Pulse 2.0, Fintech Global, Crowdfund Insider, PYMNTS, Coverager), all September 2026; the company website shows a press date of November 12, 2026, a conflict, so September is used. No seed round was found. Traction claims ($1.8B vs over $2B transactions, 10 of top 25 servicers) are company or secondary. Competitor search found only 2026 dated pages (Salient, Skit.ai), not near the Summer 2024 batch, so competition_at_founding is left empty.
